series: When the promises come due: the AI buildout's spend, financing, signed leases and carrying cost
unit: nominal US$ billions unless a field says otherwise
description: Inputs for the promises interactive (src/viz/promises.js). Measured figures are from company filings (SEC XBRL and 10-Q text, fetched 2026-10-20), the Bank of England, Bain and Epoch AI pages fetched the same day, and figures already sourced in drafts/economic-context.md and drafts/store.md. Anything that rests on secondhand reporting or on the editor's brief (drafts/scratch/army/06-money-and-buildout.md) without a re-fetch carries (v) in its note. Editorial assumptions are labeled 'assumption'.
license: Compiled for this post from the cited sources; facts only.
caveats: The model counts depreciation and interest, not power, staff or the labs' own costs; the compute share of revenue stands in for those.
Revenue is industry-wide and deduplicated, not any one company's.
The spend shape, the split of the non-Morgan-Stanley 24% of financing, the vendor rate, the fade rate and the 20-year building write-off are editorial assumptions, labeled on the page.
This is a model of promises and when they come due. It does not predict prices, defaults, or any company's solvency, and it is not financial advice.

guess_spent.note: A floor, not a total: cash purchases of property and equipment only. Excludes finance-lease additions (material at Microsoft), xAI, OpenAI's partners, Chinese and sovereign builders, and non-US filers. Not all of it is AI. Amazon's tag is PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets.

H1 2026 only, same companies (Oracle quarters ending Feb and May 2026).

chipLife.note: Chip life: the builders carry chips as lasting five or six years (10-Ks); Amazon moved part of its fleet back to five; Michael Burry argues two to three. An A100 from 2020 still rents at six years old.

hwShare.note: Bank of England, Dec 2025: AI chips 'comprise around half of AI data centre costs'.

buildingLife.note: assumption: between CoreWeave's ~12 years left on building leases and buildings that last decades (drafts/store.md).

delay.note: No source gives an industry-wide average wait; default 0. Power plants that came online in 2025 waited a median of over five years to connect (drafts/store.md).

mix.note: Morgan Stanley via the Bank of England: $2.9T 2025-28, $1.5T from external capital including $800B of private credit, so about 48% from the builders' own cash and 28% private credit (here: SPV and project debt). The split of the remaining 24% (IG bonds 12, neocloud debt 6, vendor-supported 2, outside equity 4) is the author's allocation, an assumption.

rates.note: IG: 10-year Treasury ~5.20% plus IG spread ~0.86% (Treasury par curve; ICE BofA via FRED, Oct 13-14). SPV: Hyperion's 6.58% bonds to 2049 (6.581% per IFR). Neocloud: CoreWeave's 9.625% 2032 and 9.75% 2031 notes (CNBC); they yielded 15-16% on Oct 14-15. Vendor: 8%, assumption.

r2026.note: (v) The author's interpolation of Exponential View's deduplicated series (trailing twelve months $161B in Sept 2026, run rate $276B); the EV page was not reachable for a re-check. For scale: OpenAI ~$50B run rate (FT) and Anthropic $16.8B in Q3 alone (FT, Bloomberg, Reuters).

growth.note: Epoch AI (fetched): OpenAI plus Anthropic tripled in 2024, grew more than fourfold in 2025, and 3.5x so far in 2026 ($30B to $105B combined); 3.5x = +250%.

fade.note: Assumption: each year's growth is 40% smaller than the last. At 40% revenue reaches about $1.9T in 2030; at 60% it levels off near $1T.

computeShare.note: Anthropic's reported $1.70 of revenue per $1 of compute in Q3 2026 (FT, Oct 15): 1 / 1.70 = 59%. Bain assumes sustainable capex is about 25% of revenue.

utilization.note: Share of built capacity that is rented. Base 98%: in the big markets less than two percent of data-center space is vacant (CBRE H1 2026: 1.4% primary-market vacancy; JLL about 1%, (v) not re-fetched). That is colocation space with power, not chips in use. The model scales revenue from 2027 in proportion to rented capacity.

localShare.note: Share of demand served on users' own machines by 2030, ramping from 0 in 2026. No published measure found; default 0, the reader's scenario. Related but different: open-weight models are about a third of enterprise tokens (ETR, (v)) or 11% (Menlo Ventures); most of those still run in data centers.

ms.note: Morgan Stanley via the Bank of England: of $2.9T (2025-28), $1.5T external 'across (mostly) debt and equity', including $800B from private credit.

leases_note: Undiscounted future payments under leases signed but not started. At year-end 2025 the five companies' total was $662B, which Moody's called implicit debt.

ladder.promise: loans 5-6 years against ~5-year contracts, ~12 years left on building leases, chips on a one-year cycle
ladder.numbers: CoreWeave debt $35B in June (10-Q); its notes due 2031 and 2032 fell to about 78 cents in mid-October (CNBC).

ladder.who: Private-credit funds, and the insurers and pensions behind them
ladder.holds: loans to developers, SPVs and chip-leasing vehicles
ladder.promise: chip-lease debt matched to five-year leases; long bond allocations
ladder.numbers: Morgan Stanley: $800B of the buildout from private credit (BoE). PIMCO bought $18B of Meta's Hyperion bonds (WSJ). Blackstone funds took $9B of ~$18B of subordinated debt on Anthropic's five-year TPU lease at 10% (FT, reported secondhand, (v)).

ladder.promise: construction-period loans, refinanced when a site is finished (assumption on the window)
ladder.numbers: About $1.3T of data-center debt, including $428B of utility and infrastructure loans and $225B syndicated; top lenders TD $26.8B, Goldman $16.5B, JPMorgan $13.3B; direct exposure about 0.8% of bank assets (Chicago Fed; Bisnow; American Banker).

ladder.promise: 20-year lease guarantees against a one-year product cycle
ladder.numbers: Nvidia guarantees up to $105B of OpenAI's payments on twenty-year leases for a campus in Ohio (Nvidia 10-Q); phases start in FY2029 (v).

ladder.holds: bonds on campuses leased to a hyperscaler
ladder.promise: a 2049 bond against a lease that runs four years at a time
ladder.numbers: Hyperion: $27.3B of 6.58% bonds to 2049; Meta's lease starts in 2029 and renews in four-year blocks to twenty; residual value guarantee about $28B; Meta's maximum exposure $46B (Meta 10-K and 10-Q; bond terms per IFR). $120B-plus has moved into such vehicles (FT via Quinn Emanuel, (v)).

ladder.promise: to the 2060s; over 40% of 2026 hyperscaler paper is 20 years or longer
ladder.numbers: About $220B of IG bonds from five hyperscalers in 2026 (JPMorgan, BNP via Reuters). Alphabet's long-term debt went from $12B (Dec 2024) to $101B (Jun 2026) (SEC XBRL).

ladder.holds: the residual: capex paid from operating cash flow
ladder.promise: no maturity; first to absorb any shortfall
ladder.numbers: About 48% of the buildout comes from the builders' own cash (Morgan Stanley via the BoE). Capex was 96% of the big four's operating cash flow in Q2 2026 (SEC XBRL).

ladder_note: Lit when a year with a shortfall in your scenario falls inside the rung's due window. Not sourced and left out: a dollar split of the debt by holder type (how much sits with insurers versus pensions versus banks). No source found gives one.
